Convert mixed format dates to Microsoft Excel serial dates

Source: R/OncReg.Excel.R
OR.date.Excel.Rd

Converts string dates that may be in serial (using the Microsoft Excel offset) or delimited format with a two-digit (e.g., "31/01/00") or four-digit (e.g., "31/01/2000") year into numeric serial dates. Fields may be delimited by "/", "-" or ".". Two-digit years are expanded using a specified century and pivot year.

Usage

OR.date.Excel(input, century = 20, pivot = 50, order = "dmy")

Arguments

input

String vector of dates in serial or delimited format, where fields are separated by "/", "-" or ".".

century

Numeric century used for expanding two-digit years. Default = 20.

pivot

Numeric threshold where two-digit years > pivot are expanded with century - 1. Default = 50.

order

String specifying the field order, e.g., "dmy", "ymd", or "mdy". Default = "dmy".

Value

Numeric vector of serial dates using the Microsoft Excel offset.

See also

Other other: OR.collapse(), OR.holdout(), OR.permutations(), OR.read.csv.stub(), OR.tdCox()

Examples

print(OR.date.Excel(c("31/01/00", "31-01-2000", "36556")))
#> [1] 36556 36556 36556
